test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which reproductive part(s) is/are essential for fertilisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pollen grain and ovule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Pollen grain and ovule:**
 
• Pollen grains contain the male gametes (sperm cells) of a plant.
 
• Ovules contain the female gametes (egg cells) of a plant.
 
• Fertilization occurs when a male gamete from a pollen grain fuses with a female gamete inside an ovule.
 
• This fusion results in the formation of a zygote, which develops into an embryo.
 
• Therefore, pollen grains and ovules are essential for sexual reproduction and fertilization in plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thalamus:**
 
• The thalamus is the part of a flower's receptacle that supports the other floral organs.
 
• It is the base of the flower to which sepals, petals, stamens, and pistils are attached.
 
• While it is structurally important, it does not directly participate in fertilization.
 
• The thalamus primary function is to support the other floral parts.
 
• The thalamus can, in some plants, develop into part of the fruit.
 
• **Petals:**
 
• Petals are the colorful, often showy parts of a flower.
 
• Their primary function is to attract pollinators, such as insects or birds.
 
• While they aid in the process leading to fertilization by attracting pollinators, they are not directly involved in the fusion of gametes.
 
• Petals can also protect some of the inner flower parts.
 
• Petal color and shape vary widely among plant species.
 
• **Sepal:**
 
• Sepals are the outermost whorl of floral parts, typically green and leaf-like.
 
• Their primary function is to protect the developing flower bud.
 
• They play no direct role in the process of fertilization.
 
• Sepals can also provide some level of photosynthetic activity.
 
• After the bud opens, sepals can remain, or fall off.
